input.rationale: Section 13.5 starts from the right place for us: Developments (including interface coding created solely by Corio) are owned by Corio and Commerce One assigns any claim of ownership to us, while Commerce One keeps its pre-existing materials and the Software (Section 2.8) — that matches the preferred position. The carve-out, however, flips ownership of work we create and fund to Commerce One whenever it supports those Developments on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to us. That is an assignment of our IP to the vendor with no right to exploit, which is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence). Our redline simply deletes the carve-out, leaving Commerce One's background IP protected by the opening proviso. Noted but not flagged: ownership of enhancements to the Software itself is left to future negotiation (Vendor owns its platform, so this is acceptable), and the agreement contains no express customer-data ownership sentence, which is a minor gap in this hosting arrangement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the carve-out that would transfer ownership of Developments we create and pay for to Commerce One merely because it supports them, since our playbook does not permit assignment of our IP to a vendor and there is no licence back. Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software remain its property under the opening proviso and Section 2.8.
proposal.summary: Delete the carve-out that gives Commerce One ownership of Developments created solely by Corio where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis.
